messages:
sara: ran a targeted perf-pass on the host pre-parse path — saw a surprising CPU hump during request boundary handling. attaching flame link: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/3823456789 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ravi: saw that too on the canary cluster, ~12-18% extra CPU compared to baseline when requests stream-chunk. looks correlated with smallwrite bursts.

alex: any chance it's the UTF8-normalize step? we've seen weird spikes when header parsing + normalizer run back-to-back.

sara: tried disabling normalize in a local build — CPU dropped ~6% but latency tail still bad for 512-1k token inputs. flame shows heavy stack in host-parse::frame_assembler and grpc-proto::read_loop.

michelle: ops-bot reported a regression alert during last deploy: "host-preparse CPU 15% -> 28% on canary (p95 latency +45ms)". ops-bot: @channel deploy-3823 triggered autoscale.

ops-bot: [ALERT] deploy 3823: host-preparse-concurrency spike. see metrics: https://metrics.redwood/streams/3823

ravi: reproduced with a trimmed repro: curl streaming requests with intermittent 256B chunks. stack dump attached below.

alex: paste the stack and perf counters? also include kernel selection telemetry (we log selected kernel id for decode).

ravi: ````
perf_counters: cpu_cycles=1.2e9, context_switches=430, syscalls=12000
hot_frames:
 - host::frame_assembler::coalesce_chunks
 - host::parse::proto_reader::read_next
 - grpc::server::on_data
kernel_selected: fast-attn-v2 (fallback path used intermittently)
kv_cache_hits: 82%
kv_cache_evictions: +12/min during burst
````

tim: interesting that kernel selector flips during the same window. maybe sequence-length jitter causes kernel re-eval and cold paths. if selector is evaluating per-request, that's expensive.

michelle: what's the batching heuristic during these tests? smallwrites might reduce effective batch fill and force more host-side overhead per token.

sara: batching config: target_batch_ms=8ms, max_batch_tokens=4096. with 256B streaming bursts we only hit 16-64 token per request until tail end, so batching is shallow.

alex: two immediate hypotheses: 1) frame coalescer doing memcpy-heavy smallwrite aggregation, 2) kernel selector re-evaluating and triggering a slow fallback when token counts vary. both could amplify CPU per-token.

ravi: i ran a quick patch that caches kernel choice per-connection for 200ms; cpu dropped ~4% in local. but not comfortable as long-term — could mischoose when sequence lengths change widely.

tim: can we instead change selector to be sticky per-request-id with backoff re-eval? cheaper than per-chunk eval. also consider sampling-based eval (only re-eval N% of requests).

michelle: agree. for KV cache, eviction spikes line up with the bursts. maybe our chunking churn changes cache key shape (prefix variance). need K-V key canonicalization.

sara: created a tiny repro harness and pushed to perf-ci: https://ci.redwood/runs/3823456789-repro. will run A/B: (A) sticky-selector, (B) canonicalize-kv-keys, (C) frame-coalesce opt (avoid extra memcpy for single-segment streams).

alex: quick micro-optim: in frame_assembler, avoid creating std::string for each tiny fragment; use slice-ref and append only when >512B. that knocked off ~2-3% CPU on local.

ravi: logging plan: add kernel-selector debug (sampled 1%) and emit selected_kernel_id + reason to traces. also add kv-key-normalized flag.

michelle: schedule triage sync tomorrow 10am PT to decide canary plan and rollback thresholds. tagging @eng-runtime leads. :calendar:

tim: one more note — gRPC writev path is sensitive to small batch writes. maybe switch to coalesced-writev in the proxy for streams under 1kB to reduce syscall count. measured syscalls decreased from 12000->8000 in patch.

sara: excellent. i'll iterate patches and post perf-ci results here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
